title: Ethiopian Tomato Salad
community: All of Ethiopia — the ubiquitous tomato accompaniment
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tomato Salad — ripe tomatoes sliced with onion, jalapeño, coriander, and lemon dressing. The simplest, most refreshing element on the Ethiopian table — the raw tomato's acidity cutting through the richness of the wats.
longDesc: Ethiopian tomato salad is the table's refreshing note — the raw tomatoes and lemon providing the bright acid counterpoint to the rich berbere wats. Simple, immediate, and essential.
steps: Slice tomatoes. Arrange on a plate.
chefTips: Very ripe tomatoes only — unripe tomatoes lack the sweetness and acidity.
Rest 5 minutes — salt draws out the tomato juices into the dressing.
cookingScience: Ripe tomatoes contain lycopene — a fat-soluble antioxidant. The small amount of oil in the dressing increases lycopene bioavailability dramatically compared to eating them with no fat.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland tomatoes — particularly sweet and acidic.
culturalNote: Ethiopian tomato salad is the simplest expression of what the Ethiopian table understands — that raw freshness and acidity are as important as richness and spice. Together they create the complete meal.
